title: Scraper: Extend ASRock to Threadripper / Threadripper Pro
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Extend the existing AsRockScraper to cover sTRX4 (Threadripper) and sWRX8 (Threadripper Pro) consumer-tier boards in addition to AM4/AM5.

board_class: Threadripper, ThreadripperPro.

Sockets:
- sTRX4: TRX40 Creator, TRX40 Taichi
- sTR5: TRX50 Nova, TRX50 Aqua (forthcoming Threadripper 9000 boards)
- sWRX8: WRX80 Creator, WRX80D8-2T (overlap with ASRock Rack — this issue covers consumer-tier; rack covered by #84)
- sWRX9: WRX90 WS EVO

Implementation:
- src/psp_etl/scrape/asrock.py uses Wayback CDX against download.asrock.com/BIOS/{socket}/* with a hardcoded _SOCKETS = ('AM4', 'AM5'). Audit the CDX index to see what additional folder names ASRock uses (likely 'TRX40', 'TRX50', 'WRX80', 'WRX90' — but verify).
- Update the _SOCKETS tuple and the _BIOS_URL_RE regex (currently hardcoded to AM[45]).
- Update classify_board_class mapping in src/psp_etl/ingest.py if any new socket names surface that aren't already there (sTRX4, sTR5, sWRX8 mapped; sWRX9 needs adding once ASRock publishes WRX90 boards).

Coordination with #84 (ASRock Rack): both this issue and the Rack issue touch the same CDX. Decide ownership before both PRs land — recommend doing #84 first since the Rack inventory naturally surfaces what folder names exist for sWRX8/sWRX9.

Acceptance criteria:
- Existing AM4/AM5 tests still pass
- New tests for at least one TRX40 and one WRX80 board URL parse
- CDX coverage report (count of new boards discovered) in commit message

Related: #79, #81 (parent for Threadripper sockets).
